title: Natural Language Processing (Almost) from Scratch
authors: R. Collobert, J. Weston, L. Bottou, M. Karlen, K. Kavukcuoglu, P. Kuksa
before: Each NLP task had its own pipeline of hand-engineered features.
problem: Feature engineering did not transfer between tasks and capped accuracy.
breakthrough: One network, trained on unlabelled text, producing representations that serve many tasks at once.
why: An early statement of the idea that became pretraining: learn general representations first, specialise later.
next: Word2vec, then ELMo and BERT, made the idea work at scale.
inherits: Unsupervised pretraining followed by task-specific use.
